title: 2026-10-28_Sofacy_Fysbis_Backdoor_Investigation_d47
description: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a potential compromise involving the Sofacy group's Fysbis Linux backdoor. The backdoor is known to establish command and control (C2) communication and exfiltrate data. Your mission is to investigate the compromised hosts, identify the malicious activity, and contain the threat.
outcomes: Identify and investigate suspicious services and processes
Analyze network communication for signs of C2 activity

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a potential compromise involving the Sofacy group's Fysbis Linux backdoor. The backdoor is known to establish command and control (C2) communication and exfiltrate data. Your mission is to investigate the compromised hosts, identify the malicious activity, and contain the threat.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the target host (IP: 192.168.50.5) using SSH with the username 'cyrano' and password 'Sofacy@2023'.
levels.local_content: Access the target host (IP: 192.168.50.5) using SSH with the username 'cyrano' and password 'Sofacy@2023'.

levels.title: Suspicious Service Discovery
levels.content: While monitoring the target host, you notice unusual network activity. Investigate the running services on the target host and identify any suspicious or unauthorized services.
levels.solution:
To identify the suspicious service, you can use the following command:

```bash
systemctl list-units --type=service --all
```

Look for any services that seem out of place or unfamiliar. The suspicious service is named `systemkernelservicedefender.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the status of all running services and look for any that seem out of place or unfamiliar.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the `systemctl list-units --type=service --all` command to list all running services.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Filter the list of services by their status to narrow down the suspicious ones.

levels.title: C2 Communication Discovery (Port)
levels.content: Now that you've identified the suspicious service, investigate its network activity. Determine which network port is used for the suspicious communication.
levels.solution:
To determine the network port used for the suspicious communication, you can use the following command:

```bash
ss -tulnp | grep systemkernelservicedefender
```

The service is listening on port 80.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Examine the network connections associated with the suspicious service.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the `ss -tulnp | grep systemkernelservicedefender` command to examine the network connections associated with the suspicious service.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for the port number in the output of the command.

levels.title: Lateral Movement Investigation
levels.content: Investigate if the attacker has moved laterally from the target host to other hosts in the network. Look for evidence of file transfers or remote execution.
levels.solution:
To investigate lateral movement, you can use the following command:

```bash
ps aux | grep -i transfer
```

The script used for lateral movement is named `payload-transfer.sh`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check for any scripts or services that transfer files between hosts.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the `ps aux | grep -i transfer` command to check for any scripts or services that transfer files between hosts.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for any processes that contain the word 'transfer' in their name or command line.
